title: The Breakdown of Contextual Ambiguity Resolution: Edge Cases and Vulnerabilities
text:
Despite the sophisticated ability to resolve polysemy—the challenge of determining a word's correct meaning based on surrounding text—these computational models exhibit significant failure modes. One critical vulnerability is the dependency on local context; models often struggle when global or discourse-level coherence establishes an ambiguous term in a manner that spans many paragraphs, leading to 'contextual drift.'

Furthermore, the system breaks down entirely when encountering deeply nuanced human communication, such as subtle sarcasm, irony, or novel cultural idioms. These instances rely on shared physical experience and implicit common sense rather than strictly linguistic rules or statistically probable co-occurrence vectors. Consequently, models frequently fail by defaulting to the most literal interpretation available within the limited immediate textual window, missing the intended pragmatic meaning.
